description:
The Natural Death Relief scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to provide financial assistance to the families of workers who have died due to natural causes. 

This scheme is specifically aimed at the unorganized sector workers who often lack social security and financial stability. 

The scheme was introduced by the Ministry of Labour and Employment under the Mahatma Gandhi Bunkar Bima Yojana. 

It was launched in the year 2019 to address the needs of the families left behind by deceased workers. 

The primary objective of the Natural Death Relief scheme is to provide immediate financial support to the bereaved families. 

This support is crucial in helping them cope with the loss of their primary breadwinner. 

The scheme aims to ensure that families do not face financial hardships during their time of grief. 

Under this scheme, a one-time financial assistance of ₹2 lakh is provided to the family of the deceased worker. 

This amount is intended to cover immediate expenses such as funeral costs and other financial obligations. 

The assistance is provided without any conditions or restrictions on how the funds should be used. 

To be eligible for the benefits of this scheme, the deceased worker must have been a registered member of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The worker must have contributed to the welfare fund for a minimum of 12 months prior to their death. 

The age limit for eligibility is generally set at 18 years and above for the workers. 

There is no upper age limit specified for the workers under this scheme. 

Families applying for the assistance must provide proof of the worker's death due to natural causes. 

This can include a death certificate issued by a competent authority. 

Additionally, the family must submit proof of their relationship to the deceased worker. 

This can be established through documents such as an Aadhaar card or a ration card. 

The application process for the Natural Death Relief scheme is straightforward and designed to be user-friendly. 

Families can apply for the assistance through the online portal of the respective State Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The application form requires the submission of specific details including the name of the deceased worker, their registration number, and the date of death. 

Applicants must also upload scanned copies of the required documents such as the death certificate and proof of relationship. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The processing time for the application is typically around 30 days. 

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the bank account of the applicant. 

The scheme is implemented by the respective State Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Boards. 

Each state has its own board responsible for the administration of the scheme. 

For example, the Delhi Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board oversees the implementation in Delhi. 

Contact details for these boards can usually be found on their official websites. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Indian government to enhance social security for unorganized sector workers. 

As of 2023, it is estimated that over 2 crore workers are registered under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The government has allocated significant funds to ensure the smooth operation of this scheme. 

In the financial year 2022-2023, the allocation for welfare schemes for construction workers was approximately ₹1,500 crore. 

This funding is crucial for sustaining the benefits provided under the Natural Death Relief scheme. 

The scheme also aims to raise awareness among workers about their rights and benefits. 

Regular campaigns are conducted to inform workers about the importance of registration and the benefits available to them. 

The government encourages families to ensure that their deceased members are registered with the welfare board to avail of the benefits. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also aims to provide emotional support to the families. 

Counseling services are made available to help families cope with the loss of their loved ones. 

The Natural Death Relief scheme is a vital component of the Indian government's efforts to provide social security to vulnerable sections of society. 

By offering financial assistance, the scheme helps alleviate the immediate financial burden on families. 

This support is essential in ensuring that families can maintain their livelihoods after the loss of a primary earner. 

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to improving the welfare of unorganized sector workers. 

It is a step towards creating a more inclusive social security system in India. 

Overall, the Natural Death Relief scheme is an important initiative that provides critical support to families in need. 

The financial assistance offered under this scheme plays a significant role in helping families navigate the challenges that arise after the death of a worker. 

The scheme is continuously monitored and evaluated to ensure its effectiveness and reach. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account to improve the scheme further. 

The government aims to expand the reach of the scheme to cover more workers and their families. 

Efforts are being made to streamline the application process to make it even more accessible. 

The Natural Death Relief scheme is a testament to the government's dedication to social welfare and worker rights. 

It stands as a crucial support system for families facing the loss of their loved ones in the unorganized sector. 

In conclusion, the Natural Death Relief scheme is a well-structured initiative that provides essential financial support to families of deceased workers. 

The scheme's objectives align with the broader goals of enhancing social security and welfare for unorganized sector workers in India.
